name: Deed: the Crater Cottage
description: A one-room cottage on the lip of the bell's crater, chalk-cob and thatch with a blue door somebody painted for a miller who has been dead forty years. The hearth draws badly when the wind is in the east. Signed over by the Merrowby reeve, witnessed twice, as the Vale requires.

property.name: the Crater Cottage
property.story: The miller's widow kept it swept for thirty years after there was nobody to sweep for.

name: Deed: the House on Bell Row
description: Two storeys on the row above the market, with a yellow brewer's door, a cellar that is a slice of the Toll's own lip, and a window that looks straight up the hill at the bell. Cold in the cellar, warm everywhere else. The reeve will want to know you intend to stay.

property.name: the House on Bell Row
property.story: The cellar wall is bronze. On a still night the whole house hums, and the family who built it learned to sing the note back.

name: Deed: the Canal Rooms
description: Three rooms over a chandler's on the Lantern Row canal, lime-washed, with a brass lamp bracket and a mooring ring under the window. Registered with the Tallymen, whose charter fee is folded into the price and mentioned only in the smallest hand.

property.name: the Canal Rooms
property.story: Every previous owner is listed on the deed's reverse, in the Tallymen's hand, back to the Charter. The third name from the end has been scraped out.

name: Deed: the Stilt House
description: A one-room house on six alder legs at the quiet end of the boardwalk, indigo shutters, a lantern hook, and a hatch in the floor for a boat you do not yet own. The Reed Council does not sell property so much as agree to stop asking when you will leave.

property.name: the Stilt House
property.story: The previous tenant went into the water with a lantern, as is proper, and the Council waited the customary year before speaking of the house at all.

name: Deed: the Cliff Cell
description: A room cut into the cliff below the Moot hall: drystone hearth, turf-stopped window, bone lintel over the door with a clan mark you are not entitled to and are expected to keep clean anyway. Bought from the Moot, who record the sale as a loan of stone.

property.name: the Cliff Cell
property.story: The mark over the door is Oskel. There are no Oskels left to mind, which is precisely why the Moot minds.

name: Deed: the Knot Room
description: A round room in a knot of the Grandfather, forty feet up a rope walk, with a shuttered knot-hole for a window and a floor of one enormous ring of dead heartwood. The Woodfolk have no deeds; this is a carved token and the word of three foresters, which is stronger.

property.name: the Knot Room
property.story: Count the rings in the floor and you get eleven hundred years. The Woodfolk let visitors count; it is the only sermon they preach.

name: Key: the Crater Cottage
description: Iron, worn smooth, with a blue thread through the bow.

name: Key: the House on Bell Row
description: Two keys on a ring: the door, and the cellar that is a bell.

name: Key: the Canal Rooms
description: Brass, stamped with a Tallymen tally and the number of the charter entry.

name: Key: the Stilt House
description: Bone, carved as an eel. Isseva's locks are a courtesy; the door is mostly shutter.

name: Key: the Cliff Cell
description: A short iron rod with three notches. In Kharrow Hold a lock says you are away, not that you distrust your neighbours.

name: Token: the Knot Room
description: A disc of black ash with three foresters' marks burnt into it. Not a key. Shown, not turned.
